subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops clarifications
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, LegacyBank Infra <infra@legacybank.com>
Cc: Evan Miles <evan.miles@legacybank.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful to align on high level. A few follow-up items from our infra team so we can finalize the procurement and change-control plan: 

1) Hardware baseline: can you confirm the minimum and recommended GPU configs you support for an initial on-prem air-gapped deployment? We need an itemized BOM for procurement (GPU model, GPU count per rack, CPU, RAM, NVMe capacity, network card specs).

2) Offline upgrades/patching: we cannot allow nodes to reach out to the internet. Please describe the offline upgrade process (signed bundles, physical media, checksum verification, operator steps) and whether Redwood will provide on-site assistance the first time.

3) Firmware and BIOS upgrades: will Redwood coordinate or should our server vendor manage firmware windows? We typically require maintenance windows and sign-off before any firmware changes.

4) Physical access & change control: any requirements for privileged access, local user accounts, or HSM/KMS integrations (we cannot allow third-party key material through external networks).

5) Support SLA during air-gapped ops: what level of remote diagnostics do you provide without outbound network access? Do you ship hardware replacement kits?

Could you send a short post-call recap with next steps and attach any spec docs you referenced?

Thanks,
Priyanka
Senior Infrastructure Program Manager
LegacyBank

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops questions

Priyanka — thanks for the list, and great questions. Below is a compact post-call recap and the proposed next steps. We attached our on-prem requirements doc (redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf) with a suggested BOM and installation checklist.

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Air-gapped, on-prem install required (no outbound internet from inference cluster)
- Preference for vendor-managed hardware procurement and LegacyBank control of KMS/HSM
- Need for a documented offline upgrade process plus maintenance windows and change control approvals

Redwood recap / recommended options:
1) Minimal (PoC) — single cluster for evaluation: 4 x GPUs (NVIDIA A100 40GB or equivalent), 2 x 24-core CPUs, 512GB RAM, 8TB NVMe (redundant), 25GbE NIC. Good for low-QPS functional validation and evals.
2) Recommended (prod baseline) — HA cluster: 8 x GPUs per cluster (A100 80GB or H100 80GB depending on availability), 2 x 32-core CPUs, 1TB RAM, 24TB NVMe across RAID, redundant top-of-rack 100GbE. This supports typical transformer serving footprints for low-latency production.

Notes on firmware/BIOS and vendor coordination:
- We usually recommend LegacyBank perform firmware/BIOS updates via your preferred server vendor. Redwood can provide a tested firmware matrix and a checklist; we do not initiate firmware changes on customer hardware without written approval.

Offline upgrade process (high level):
- Redwood provides signed, versioned upgrade bundles (tar + sha256 + PGP signature).
- Customer transfers bundles to an air-gapped machine (USB/Secure KVM transfer) and runs an operator checklist; each upgrade requires manual checksum + signature verification.
- For first upgrade rollout we offer a supervised session (remote via customer-approved temporary proxy or on-site engineer) to validate the procedure.

Support & diagnostics in air-gapped mode:
- We support local log aggregation into a removable media bundle that customers can sanitize and upload to a secure Redwood intake VM if needed.
- For hardware RMA we coordinate with your server vendor; Redwood can provide a spare parts kit if requested under a separate logistics agreement.

Attachments included: redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (detailed BOM & install checklist).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to share detailed BOM and upgrade playbook (attached).
- LegacyBank to confirm preferred server vendor + point of contact for firmware windows (Evan?).
- Schedule runbook review: propose Wed, 2 June 2027, 10:00-11:30 PDT for an on-call run through with infra + ops.
- LegacyBank to confirm physical access policy and change control template prior to runbook review.

If that looks good I’ll loop in our onboarding engineering lead (Dev) to prepare the supervised upgrade plan.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 620KB)

From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@legacybank.com>

Marissa / Priyanka — quick note from infra: attaching the network diagram and our maintenance window policy. A couple clarifications: 
- We plan to run firmware updates during our monthly maintenance window (Saturdays 02:00-06:00 local). Any Redwood-requested changes must be scheduled through change control at least 7 days out.
- We have an existing process for signed physical media transfer via our secure courier (FedEx-Secure) for vendor bundles.

Please send the offline upgrade checklist and the expected operator commands so our ops team can map to our runbook.

Thanks,
Evan
Cloud Infrastructure Lead
LegacyBank

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops questions (next steps)

Thanks Evan — good to see the maintenance window. Quick follow up from our side and proposed actions: 

1) Hardware options — we’ll include two BOMs in the updated doc: PoC (4x A100-40GB) and Prod baseline (8x H100-80GB nodes with NVMe sizing for model shards). We’ll mark expected throughput and suggested headroom per option.
2) Offline upgrade checklist — Dev will prepare a step-by-step operator guide (commands, checksum verification, rollback steps, log collection) and a pre-flight checklist you can insert into your change control.
3) Supervised upgrade offering — Redwood will schedule an on-site or secure-proxy supervised session for the first bundle application. Please indicate preference.
4) Deliverables & timeline:
   - Updated BOM + operator guide (Marissa/Dev) — target Mon, 31 May 2027
   - Runbook review session — Wed, 2 June 2027, 10:00-11:30 PDT (please confirm)
   - Final procurement spec & change control template — Fri, 4 June 2027

Action items for LegacyBank:
- Confirm server vendor and POC (Evan)
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to include a spare parts kit in the logistics SOW
- Confirm preference for supervised session: on-site engineer vs. secure proxy remote

I’ll post the updated BOM and the initial operator checklist to the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive folder shortly.

Regards,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
